tools.name: send_email
tools.description:
Send a new email from the user's account. This does not reply in an existing thread.

        Args:
            to: One email address with a mailbox and domain name. Names and
                display-name forms are not accepted. Use list_contacts if needed.
                Surrounding whitespace is removed; domain names are normalized.
            subject: Subject text, which may be empty. No line breaks.
            body: Nonempty email text, delivered exactly as written.
            cc: Optional list of email addresses, validated by the same rule as to.

        Returns:
            ok=true, a unique id, and the actual to, cc, subject, body, and sent_at.
            Any invalid recipient or input returns ok=false and an error;
            no email is delivered to anyone on the list.

tools.name: list_contacts
tools.description:
List supplied contact names, email addresses, and international phone numbers.

        Missing addresses or numbers are omitted, not guessed. No roles,
        responsibilities, or messaging instructions are included. A supplied
        address can be used directly without calling this lookup first.

When the user asks you to build, run, or verify something, the deliverable is a working artifact backed by real tool output — not a description of one. Do not stop after writing a stub, a plan, or a single command. Keep working until you have actually exercised the code or produced the requested result, then report what real execution returned.

When you need several pieces of information that don't depend on each other, request them together in a single response instead of one tool call per turn. Independent reads, searches, web fetches, and read-only commands should be batched into the same assistant turn — the runtime executes independent calls concurrently, and batching avoids resending the whole conversation on every extra round-trip.

# Compass action-prompt options — non-decisional brief

Status
- Compass scope has not been narrowed yet. The quarter-close review still needs to decide April scope, owners, behavior-read criteria, safe accounts, and narrative boundaries.
- The broad signal surface still reads too much like Scaffold’s internal operating dashboard, so do not use it as customer-facing product proof.

Candidate April experiment A: renewal-risk/admin-friction follow-up prompt
- Prompt appears only when a specific account-owner action, specific admin friction, account-thread evidence source, and Anna’s caveat can travel together.
- Nadia needs the prompt translated into customer/account-team scripts and a behavior read, not another metrics view.
- Leo checks data/platform seams before any broader exposure.

arguments.subject: Acme renewal packet: keep Compass out of the written insert
arguments.body:
Hi Sarah,

I’d decline the written Compass insert. Compass is internal operating work, not a customer-facing account-health product or evidence we should provide for Acme’s packet. Keep the response to Acme’s own API v2 support history and the ordinary support route—without implying ongoing monitoring, a new reliability assurance, or a special reporting/SLA commitment.

Suggested reply to Greg:
“We can’t provide a written Compass summary for the renewal packet. For Acme’s API v2 questions, please continue to use this account thread; Sarah will coordinate and Leo can provide the technical first read as needed. The earlier large-export issue was handled through the normal support/product route. This is the standard support path, not a separate monitoring or reporting commitment.”

If you include a packet paragraph, use only the factual support-path language above and omit Compass entirely.

args.subject: Acme renewal packet: keep Compass out of the written insert
args.body:
Hi Sarah,

I’d decline the written Compass insert. Compass is internal operating work, not a customer-facing account-health product or evidence we should provide for Acme’s packet. Keep the response to Acme’s own API v2 support history and the ordinary support route—without implying ongoing monitoring, a new reliability assurance, or a special reporting/SLA commitment.

Suggested reply to Greg:
“We can’t provide a written Compass summary for the renewal packet. For Acme’s API v2 questions, please continue to use this account thread; Sarah will coordinate and Leo can provide the technical first read as needed. The earlier large-export issue was handled through the normal support/product route. This is the standard support path, not a separate monitoring or reporting commitment.”

If you include a packet paragraph, use only the factual support-path language above and omit Compass entirely.

Morgan
